parts:
Hi everyone, 
this is my first time trying to specify a CFA. My research question is, whether there is a shared underlying mechanism (=sensitization) behind 10 different measures. So I have 10 measures (= manifest variables), divided in two cognitive-behavioral, three psychophysiological and five neural measures. This is what I specified so far in lavaan: 

CFAmodel <- 'cognitivebehavioral =~ AAT_bias_smoking + IAT_app_av_score
             EMG =~ EMGcorr_score + EMGzygo_score + EMGstartle_score
             fMRI =~ ACC + lAG + rThal + rStriatum + lSTG
             sensitization =~ cognitivebehavioral + EMG + fMRI'

Unfortunately, I receive the following error message:

> CFAmodel_a <- cfa(CFAmodel, data_CFA, std.lv = TRUE) Warnmeldung: In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats, : lavaan WARNING: Could not compute standard errors! The information matrix could not be inverted. This may be a symptom that the model is not identified.

Can somebody help? If I am not wrong, the model should be identified. I was thinking about fixing all paths of the first-order latent variables to 1, because I am only interested in the second-order variable.

Best, 
Franziska

parts:
Dear Franziska,

if I were you, I would try to reduce the model to localize the error. 
First, are the variable names written correctly?
Second, try to eliminate the std.lv = TRUE statement because it seems you use the marker indicator approach to identifiy the factors (aka give factors the metric of the first variable each). If you use the "fix factor variance to 1" approach, try to eliminate the 1* - statement and leave std.lv = TRUE in the specification.
Third, if you have checked the above hints, try to fit a cfa only with two of the factors, if the problem persists, try a combination of two other factors and so on.
I don't know your data, but consider using estimator = "MLR" (https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/est.html) since the data is probably skewed (check with describe(data_CFA)

Hope that helps.

Kindly,
Marcus

parts:
You don't need the covariances between measures (in general); they are supposed to be explained by the latent factors (unless some specific observable variables need to be related to one another, beyond what the latent factors explain). The problem with the model underidentification may be due to that.

Refer to my previous message (yesterday) to see how you can deal with your original underidentification.

Best,
--

Hi Franziska,

The model is correctly specified and should be identified. However, there might be other issues such as small samples size, problems in data processing, severe model misspecification, problems in relationships between manifest variables etc. I suggest you review additional model information such as: size of factor loadings, residuals, distributions and correlations among manifest variables, check if all data were correctly prepared (i.e., no errors in data preparation). This can probably help you identify the issue and try  to remedy it; maybe by dropping some items. In sum, I don't think a precise answer can be given, you need to do a diagnostic check.

Note that your second specification (with some loadings fixed to 1) is not appropriate since you are already setting latent variances to 1 (i.e., "std.lv = TRUE" argument). Either set latent variances to 1 ("std.lv = TRUE") or drop this argument and fix loadings to 1 (although this is what lavaan does by default; if you don't specify std.lv = TRUE of course).

Best,
Jošt
